title: Choose by kind with match
objective: Use match with when to run different code for each kind of value, and read values out of a kind.

body.text: match looks at a value and runs the first when that fits. Each when names a kind from a kind declaration, and the lines under it run only for that kind. The first example has a kind called light with three choices.

body.title: Match a kind
body.code:
kind light
    is a red
    is a yellow
    is a green

make signal equal to a red
match signal
    when red
        say "stop"
    when yellow
        say "wait"
    when green
        say "go"

body.text: A kind can carry values. When a choice has fields, a when can name the choice and give each value its own name with with, so the lines inside can use it. Here a circle's radius is read into r.

body.title: Read values in a when
body.code:
kind shape
    is a circle with radius of type number
    is a rectangle with width of type number and height of type number
    is a blank

make s equal to a circle with radius 3
match s
    when a circle with radius r
        say "circle of radius {r}"
    when a rectangle with width w and height h
        say "rectangle"
    when blank
        say "empty"

body.text: match works on an option too. A when nothing branch handles the missing case, and when something with value name gives the value a name inside the branch.

body.title: Match an option
body.code:
make maybe name equal to nothing of type text?
match maybe name
    when nothing
        say "missing"
    when something with value name
        say name

body.prompt: The reply is a no, but the match has no branch for that kind, so the program does not compile. Make it print rejected.
body.starter:
kind answer
    is a yes
    is a no

make reply equal to a no
match reply
    when yes
        say "accepted"
body.solution:
kind answer
    is a yes
    is a no

make reply equal to a no
match reply
    when yes
        say "accepted"
    when no
        say "rejected"
